attractions.name: Clock Tower (Ghanta Ghar) & the Eight Bazaars
attractions.description: A colonial-era clock tower at the center of Faisalabad's distinctive eight radiating bazaars, modeled after the Union Jack layout.

attractions.name: Lyallpur Museum
attractions.description: A museum documenting Faisalabad's history under its former name Lyallpur, and its growth as a textile hub.

attractions.name: Jinnah Garden (Company Bagh)
attractions.description: A large public park in the city center, popular for family outings and evening walks.

attractions.name: Chenab Club
attractions.description: A historic colonial-era social club reflecting Faisalabad's British-era planning as an agricultural and trade hub.

attractions.name: D-Ground
attractions.description: A popular modern hangout and dining strip with restaurants, cafes, and shops.

food_places.name: D-Ground food street restaurants
food_places.specialty: Wide variety of restaurants popular with families and students

food_places.name: Vegetable Market (Sabzi Mandi) food stalls
food_places.specialty: Cheap and authentic local street food

food_places.name: Salt'n Pepper Faisalabad
food_places.specialty: Popular family restaurant chain with a broad menu

food_places.name: Traditional karahi houses near Susan Road

transportation.notes: Frequent departures, also served by train
Convenient for reaching the clock tower and D-Ground areas
Cheapest local option, though less frequent than in Lahore/Karachi

weather_info.climate_type: Semi-arid, continental climate with hot summers and cool winters
weather_info.avoid_months: May to July (very hot and dry, often 42°C+)

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Moderate rainfall, occasional waterlogging in low areas

travel_tips.tip: Use the Faisalabad-Sargodha Road bypass or the Canal Road to avoid the busy eight-bazaar city center when crossing town.
Ride-hailing apps are widely available and generally the easiest way to get around as a visitor.
Winter mornings can bring dense fog/smog affecting visibility and travel times; check conditions before early departures.
Visit the Clock Tower and surrounding bazaars in the morning before it gets too crowded and hot, and save D-Ground for the evening.

history.founded: Founded in 1892 by the British as 'Lyallpur', named after Punjab Lieutenant-Governor James Lyall
history.city_history: Faisalabad was planned by the British as a model agricultural town, with its famous eight bazaars radiating from a central clock tower in a pattern resembling the Union Jack. It was renamed Faisalabad in 1979 in honor of Saudi King Faisal, and grew into Pakistan's major textile and industrial hub, earning the nickname 'Manchester of Pakistan'.
history.province_history: Punjab, meaning 'land of five rivers', has one of the longest continuous histories in South Asia, home to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa), later ruled by the Mauryas, Mughals, Sikh Empire, and the British before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947.
